issues.body: find_ingestion_rejections() now uses created_jobs() for cancelled_above candidates, but the primary newest action_required run is still cleared by `if isinstance(jobs, int) and jobs > 0`. In Python, True satisfies that expression. The --state-file route preserves JSON booleans, so a job_counts entry of true for the rejected run is classified as approval-gated-with-jobs and emits no finding despite lacking a measured positive job count. The new boolean tests cover created_jobs() and cancelled_above only; they do not exercise this primary mute branch or its JSON state-file seam.
issues.fix_hint: Replace the primary positive-job predicate with created_jobs(jobs). Ensure zero-versus-unreadable classification and finding serialization also treat booleans as unreadable rather than numeric. Add a detector test whose newest action_required run has its own count set to True and an end-to-end --state-file test with JSON true; both must keep the alert open and classify the count as unreadable.
issues.title: Boolean job count still clears the primary rejection path

verdict.summary: The round-3 major remains materially unchanged. The new created_jobs() helper correctly excludes JSON booleans and is used for cancelled-run recovery evidence, but the primary action_required job-count branch still uses isinstance(jobs, int) and jobs > 0. Because bool is a subclass of int, a state-file value of true still suppresses a live ingestion-rejection finding as approval-gated-with-jobs. The added boolean detector coverage exercises only cancelled_above; there is still no primary-branch or end-to-end state-file regression row for the exact prior finding. With the same major present at the same severity, progress is stagnant.
